title: Interest Days on Internal Appeals for Late Adjudication — Insurance Coverage & Claims Appeals Timetable
content:
**Appeals timetable — Insurance Coverage & Claims, internal appeals filed by Halverson Clinical Laboratories with contracted commercial plans.**

The internal appeal's interest days depend on how long the plan took to adjudicate the claim, measured in calendar days between the claim's filing date and its denial date (the latest denial date on the claim), compared with the expected adjudication period of the coverage's payer class:

1. Where the plan took **more than twice** its expected adjudication days, interest runs for every calendar day from the filing date to today.
2. Where the plan took **more than** its expected adjudication days but not more than twice that, interest runs for the calendar days from the filing date to today less the expected adjudication days.
3. Otherwise no interest runs.

## Expected adjudication periods

| Payer class | Expected adjudication period (calendar days of filing) | More than this | More than twice this |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Medicare Supplement Plan | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial In-Network Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | 45 | 46 or more days | 91 or more days |

## Worked days (hypothetical claim, expected adjudication period 30 days, today is 200 calendar days after filing)

| Filing date to denial date | Band | Interest days |
|---|---|---|
| 75 days | More than twice 30 | 200 |
| 61 days | More than twice 30 | 200 |
| 60 days | More than 30, not more than 60 | 200 less 30, that is 170 |
| 31 days | More than 30, not more than 60 | 170 |
| 30 days | Not more than 30 | 0 |
